prompt: If one removes some $1\times1\times1$ cubes from a $5\times5\times5$ cube, one obtains the solid shown. It consists of several equally high pillars that are built upon a common base. How many little cubes have been removed?

solutions.title: Count the removed columns
solutions.body:
The base is a full $5\times 5$ layer. On top of it, in the $5\times5$ grid of columns, pillars stand at every second position in both directions: rows 1, 3, 5 and columns 1, 3, 5, i.e. $3\cdot 3 = 9$ pillars. The other $25 - 9 = 16$ columns have lost their top 4 cubes each: $16\cdot 4 = 64$ cubes removed.

**Answer: (C) 64**

solutions.title: Count what is left
solutions.body:
What remains: the base ($25$ cubes) plus 9 pillars of height 4 above it ($36$ cubes), i.e. $61$ cubes. Removed: $125 - 61 = 64$.

**Answer: (C) 64**

prompt: Today is Carmen, Gerda and Sabine's birthday. The sum of their ages is now 44. What will the sum of their ages be the next time it is a two-digit number with two equal digits?

solutions.title: Add 3 per year
solutions.body:
Each year the sum grows by 3, so the future sums are $44 + 3t$, which leave remainder 2 when divided by 3. Check: $55$ (remainder 1), $66$ (remainder 0), $77$ (remainder 2) ✓. So after $t = 11$ years the sum is $77$.

**Answer: (C) 77**

prompt: What is the value of $a^{-3k}$, if $a^k = \frac12$?

In three differently sized baskets there are 48 balls in total. Together, the smallest and the biggest basket hold twice as many balls as the middle one. The smallest basket holds half as many balls as the middle one. How many balls are there in the biggest basket?

solutions.title: Middle basket first
solutions.body:
If the middle basket holds $m$, the other two together hold $2m$, so $3m = 48$ and $m = 16$. The smallest holds $8$, so the biggest holds $32 - 8 = 24$.

**Answer: (C) 24**

solutions.title: Scale
solutions.body:
The numerator is exactly twice the denominator, since $2^{2014} = 2\cdot 2^{2013}$ and $2^{2013} = 2\cdot 2^{2012}$.

**Answer: (E) 2**

prompt: For which of the following expressions is $b + 1$ not a factor?
How many digits does the result of the calculation $(2^{22})^5\times(5^{55})^2$ have?

solutions.title: Powers of 10
solutions.body:
$(2^{22})^5 = 2^{110}$ and $(5^{55})^2 = 5^{110}$, so the product is $10^{110}$: a 1 followed by 110 zeros, which has 111 digits.

**Answer: (E) 111**

prompt: Handsome Fritz has a secret e-mail address which is only known by four of his friends. Today he received eight e-mails at this address. Which of the following statements is definitely correct?

choices.text: Fritz has received two e-mails from each friend.
Fritz cannot have received eight e-mails from one friend.
Fritz has received at least one e-mail from each friend.
Fritz has received at least two e-mails from one of his friends.
Fritz has received at least two e-mails from at least two of his friends.

solutions.title: Pigeonhole
solutions.body:
If every friend had sent at most one e-mail, there would be at most 4 e-mails. With 8 e-mails, some friend sent at least 2, so (D) is certain.

The others can fail: all 8 could come from one friend, which contradicts (A), (B), (C) and (E).

**Answer: (D)**

prompt: The curved surfaces of two identical cylinders are cut open along the vertical dotted line, as shown, and then stuck together to create the curved surface of one big cylinder. What can be said about the volume of the resulting cylinder compared to the volume of one of the small cylinders?

solutions.title: Radius doubles
solutions.body:
The big cylinder has the same height and twice the circumference, so twice the radius. Volume $\pi r^2h$ grows with the square of the radius: $2^2 = 4$ times as big.

**Answer: (D)**

prompt: In the year 2014 all digits are different and the last digit is bigger than the sum of the other three digits. How many years ago was this last the case?

solutions.title: Search backwards
solutions.body:
Years $2000$–$2013$ fail (repeated digits, or $3 \not> 2 + 0 + 1$ for 2013). For years $1abc$ we need $c > 1 + a + b$ with $c \le 9$, so $a + b \le 7$. To get the latest year make $a$ as large as possible: $a = 7$, $b = 0$, $c = 9$ gives $1709$ (digits 1, 7, 0, 9 all different, $9 > 8$). With $a = 8$ or $9$ it is impossible. So the last such year was 1709, and $2014 - 1709 = 305$.

**Answer: (C) 305**

prompt: A cuboid-shaped box has the measurements $a\times b\times c$ with $a < b < c$. If one increases $a$ or $b$ or $c$ by 5 cm, the volume of the box increases as well. When is the increase biggest?

choices.text: The answer depends on the values of $a$, $b$ and $c$.
The volume increases in the cases (A), (B) and (C) by an equal amount.

solutions.title: Compare the increases
solutions.body:
Increasing $a$ by 5 adds $5bc$; increasing $b$ adds $5ac$; increasing $c$ adds $5ab$. Since $a < b < c$, the product $bc$ is the largest: $bc > ac > ab$. So increasing the smallest edge $a$ gives the biggest increase.

**Answer: (A)**

prompt: The winning team of a football match gets 3 points and the losing team 0 points. In the case of a draw both teams get one point each. Four teams A, B, C and D play a tournament. Each team plays each other team exactly once. At the end of the tournament Team A has 7 points, and Teams B and C have 4 points each. How many points has Team D got?

solutions.title: Count wins and draws
solutions.body:
Each team plays 3 games. 7 points from 3 games means 2 wins and 1 draw (A). 4 points means 1 win, 1 draw, 1 loss (B and C).

So A, B, C together have 4 wins and 3 draw-results. Each draw gives a draw-result to two teams, so the total number of draw-results is even: D has an odd number of draws, 1 or 3.

There are 6 games. If D had 3 draws, there would be 3 drawn games and only 3 decided games — but there are already 4 wins. So D has 1 draw, there are 2 drawn games and 4 decided games, all won by A, B, C. D has 0 wins and 1 draw: **1 point**.

**Answer: (B) 1**

solutions.title: Total points
solutions.body:
With $d$ drawn games the total is $3\cdot 6 - d = 18 - d$ points. A, B, C have $15$, so D has $3 - d$. A, B, C have 3 draws among them; D's draws make the total of draw-results $2d$. $d = 2$: D has 1 draw and $3 - 2 = 1$ point (consistent). $d = 3$: D would have 0 points but 3 draws (3 points) — contradiction. $d \le 1$ is impossible since A, B, C already have 3 draw-results.

**Answer: (B) 1**

prompt: The ratio of the radii of two concentric circles is $1:3$. The line $AC$ is a diameter of the bigger circle. A chord $BC$ of the big circle touches the small circle (see diagram). The line $AB$ has length 12. What is the radius of the big circle?

solutions.title: Midline of the triangle
solutions.body:
$AC$ is a diameter, so $\angle ABC = 90^\circ$ (Thales), i.e. $AB \perp BC$. Let $O$ be the centre and $T$ the point where $BC$ touches the small circle; $OT \perp BC$, so $OT \parallel AB$. Since $O$ is the midpoint of $AC$, $OT$ is a midline of triangle $ABC$: $OT = \frac{AB}{2} = 6$.

So the small radius is 6 and the big radius is $3\cdot 6 = 18$.

**Answer: (B) 18**

solutions.title: Pythagoras
solutions.body:
Let the radii be $r$ and $3r$. In triangle $OTC$: $TC^2 = 9r^2 - r^2 = 8r^2$, and $T$ is the midpoint of $BC$, so $BC^2 = 32r^2$. In the right triangle $ABC$: $12^2 + 32r^2 = (6r)^2 = 36r^2$, so $4r^2 = 144$, $r = 6$, and the big radius is $18$.

**Answer: (B) 18**

prompt: How many whole-number triples $(a, b, c)$ with $a > b > c > 1$ fulfil the condition $\frac1a + \frac1b + \frac1c > 1$?

solutions.title: Bound the smallest numbers
solutions.body:
If $c \ge 3$ then $b \ge 4$, $a \ge 5$ and the sum is at most $\frac13 + \frac14 + \frac15 < 1$. So $c = 2$, and we need $\frac1a + \frac1b > \frac12$ with $a > b \ge 3$.

- $b = 3$: $\frac1a > \frac16$, so $a < 6$: $a = 4$ or $5$.
- $b \ge 4$: $\frac1a + \frac1b < \frac14 + \frac14 = \frac12$. ✗

Two triples: $(4, 3, 2)$ and $(5, 3, 2)$.

**Answer: (C) 2**

prompt: Six weeks are $n!$ ($= n\cdot(n-1)\cdot\ldots\cdot 2\cdot 1$) seconds. $n = \,?$

solutions.title: Factor the seconds
solutions.body:
Six weeks in seconds: $6\cdot 7\cdot 24\cdot 60\cdot 60$. Write $24 = 8\cdot 3$, $60\cdot 60 = 3600 = 2\cdot 4\cdot 5\cdot 9\cdot 10$:

$$6\cdot 7\cdot 8\cdot 3\cdot 2\cdot 4\cdot 5\cdot 9\cdot 10 = 10!$$

**Answer: (D) 10**

prompt: The vertices of a die are numbered 1 to 8, so that the sum of the four numbers on the vertices of each face are the same. The numbers 1, 4 and 6 are already indicated in the picture. Which number is in position $x$?

solutions.title: Face sums
solutions.body:
Each vertex belongs to 3 faces, so the six face sums add up to $3(1 + 2 + \dots + 8) = 108$: every face has sum $18$.

The bottom face contains 1, 4, 6 and the fourth bottom vertex, which must be $18 - 11 = 7$ (it is below $x$, diagonally opposite to 1 on the bottom).

Let the top vertices be $p$ (above 1), $q$ (above 4), $r$ (above 6) and $x$ (above 7). Faces: front $1 + 4 + p + q = 18$, right $4 + 7 + q + x = 18$, back $6 + 7 + r + x = 18$. So $p + q = 13$, $q + x = 7$, $r + x = 5$, using the remaining numbers $2, 3, 5, 8$.

$q + x = 7$ needs $\{q, x\} = \{2, 5\}$. If $q = 2$, then $p = 11$ ✗. So $q = 5$, $x = 2$, $p = 8$, $r = 3$. Check the left face: $1 + 6 + 8 + 3 = 18$ ✓.

**Answer: (A) 2**

prompt: On the packaging of a soft cheese it says: total amount of fat 24%. On the same packaging it also says: 64% fat in the dry substance. What percentage of the soft cheese is water?

solutions.title: Find the dry part
solutions.body:
Take 100 g of cheese: 24 g fat. These 24 g are 64% of the dry substance, so the dry substance weighs $\frac{24}{0.64} = 37.5$ g. The rest, $100 - 37.5 = 62.5$ g, is water.

**Answer: (B) 62.5 %**

prompt: The function $f(x) = ax + b$ fulfils the conditions $f(f(f(1))) = 29$ and $f(f(f(0))) = 2$. What is the value of $a$?

solutions.title: Compose
solutions.body:
$f(f(f(x))) = a^3x + (a^2 + a + 1)b$. Subtracting the two conditions: $a^3(1 - 0) = 29 - 2 = 27$, so $a = 3$.

**Answer: (C) 3**

solutions.title: Differences
solutions.body:
A linear function multiplies differences by $a$: $f(u) - f(v) = a(u - v)$. Applying $f$ three times to $1$ and $0$ multiplies their difference 1 by $a^3$: $a^3 = 29 - 2 = 27$, $a = 3$.

**Answer: (C) 3**

prompt: Amongst 10 different positive whole numbers there are exactly 5 that are divisible by 5 and exactly 7 that are divisible by 7. Let $M$ be the biggest amongst these numbers. What is the smallest possible value of $M$?

solutions.title: Overlap is forced
solutions.body:
Only 10 numbers, but $5 + 7 = 12$ divisibility properties: at least 2 numbers are divisible by both 5 and 7, i.e. by 35. Two different multiples of 35 means one of them is at least 70, so $M \ge 70$.

$M = 70$ works: $35, 70$ (both), $7, 14, 21, 28, 42$ (multiples of 7 only), $5, 10, 15$ (multiples of 5 only). That's 10 numbers, 5 divisible by 5, 7 divisible by 7, maximum 70. Since 70 is not among (A)–(D):

**Answer: (E) another value**

prompt: $PQRS$ is a rectangle. $T$ is the midpoint of $RS$. $QT$ is perpendicular to the diagonal $PR$. What is the ratio of the lengths $PQ : QR$?

solutions.title: Dot product
solutions.body:
Let $P = (0,0)$, $Q = (w,0)$, $R = (w,h)$, $S = (0,h)$, $T = (\frac w2, h)$. Then $\vec{QT} = (-\frac w2, h)$ and $\vec{PR} = (w, h)$. Perpendicular: $-\frac{w^2}{2} + h^2 = 0$, so $w^2 = 2h^2$ and $PQ : QR = w : h = \sqrt2 : 1$.

**Answer: (D)**

solutions.title: Similar triangles
solutions.body:
Since $QT \perp PR$, $\angle RQT = 90^\circ - \angle QRP = \angle QPR$. So triangles $PQR$ and $QRT$ (right angles at $Q$ and $R$) are similar: $\frac{RT}{QR} = \frac{QR}{PQ}$. With $RT = \frac{PQ}{2}$: $QR^2 = \frac{PQ^2}{2}$, i.e. $PQ : QR = \sqrt2 : 1$.

**Answer: (D)**

prompt: Let $a, b, c$ be different real numbers not equal to zero and $n$ be a positive whole number. It is known that the numbers $(-2)^{2n+3}\times a^{2n+2}\times b^{2n-1}\times c^{3n+2}$ and $(-3)^{2n+2}\times a^{4n+1}\times b^{2n+5}\times c^{3n-4}$ have the same sign. Which of the following statements is definitely true?

solutions.title: Compare sign factors
solutions.body:
Look at the sign of each factor.

- First number: $(-2)^{\text{odd}} < 0$; $a^{\text{even}} > 0$; $b^{2n-1}$ has the sign of $b$; $c^{3n+2}$ has some sign $\sigma$.
- Second number: $(-3)^{\text{even}} > 0$; $a^{4n+1}$ has the sign of $a$; $b^{2n+5}$ has the sign of $b$; $c^{3n-4}$ has the same sign $\sigma$, since $3n+2$ and $3n-4$ differ by 6 (same parity).

Equal signs means $-\,\text{sgn}(b)\,\sigma = \text{sgn}(a)\,\text{sgn}(b)\,\sigma$, i.e. $\text{sgn}(a) = -1$: $a < 0$. Nothing follows for $b$ or $c$.

**Answer: (D)**

solutions.title: Divide
solutions.body:
Both numbers have the same sign exactly when their quotient is positive. The quotient is

$$\frac{(-2)^{2n+3}}{(-3)^{2n+2}}\cdot a^{-2n+1}\cdot b^{-6}\cdot c^{6},$$

where $b^{-6}c^6 > 0$ and the first fraction is negative. So $a^{1-2n}$ (an odd power of $a$) must be negative: $a < 0$.

**Answer: (D)**

prompt: The straight line $g$ runs through the vertex $A$ of the rectangle $ABCD$ shown. The perpendicular distance from $C$ to $g$ is 2 and from $D$ to $g$ is 6. $AD$ is twice as long as $AB$. Determine the length of $AD$.

solutions.title: Coordinates
solutions.body:
Put $A = (0,0)$, $D = (2s, 0)$, $C = (2s, s)$, $B = (0, s)$, and let $g$ have direction $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$. The distance from a point $(x, y)$ to $g$ is $|x\sin\theta - y\cos\theta|$.

- $D$: $2s\sin\theta = 6$, so $s\sin\theta = 3$.
- $C$ (below $g$, as in the picture): $2s\sin\theta - s\cos\theta = 2$, so $s\cos\theta = 4$.

Then $s^2 = 3^2 + 4^2 = 25$, $s = 5$ and $AD = 10$. (Check: $g$ meets $BC$ at $x = s\cot\theta = \frac{20}{3} < 10$, as drawn.)

**Answer: (A) 10**

prompt: There are 9 kangaroos that are called the Greatkangs. They are either coloured white or black. If three Greatkangs meet by chance, the probability that none of them is white is exactly two thirds. How many Greatkangs are black?

solutions.title: Count triples
solutions.body:
With $k$ black ones, $P(\text{all three black}) = \binom{k}{3}\big/\binom{9}{3} = \frac{\binom k3}{84} = \frac23$, so $\binom k3 = 56 = \binom 83$. Hence $k = 8$.

**Answer: (E) 8**

solutions.title: Check the options
solutions.body:
$k = 8$: $\frac{8}{9}\cdot\frac{7}{8}\cdot\frac{6}{7} = \frac{6}{9} = \frac23$ ✓. For $k = 6$: $\frac69\cdot\frac58\cdot\frac47 = \frac{5}{21}$ ✗; smaller $k$ give even smaller probabilities.

**Answer: (E) 8**

prompt: In the diagram on the right the following can be seen: a straight line, which is the common tangent of two touching circles with radius 1, and a square with one edge on the straight line and the other vertices one on each of the two circles. What is the side length of the square?

solutions.title: Coordinates
solutions.body:
Let the line be the $x$-axis and the circles have centres $(\pm1, 1)$; they touch at $(0, 1)$ above the point $(0,0)$. By symmetry the square is $[-\frac s2, \frac s2]\times[0, s]$. Its top right corner $(\frac s2, s)$ lies on the right circle:

$$\left(\tfrac s2 - 1\right)^2 + (s - 1)^2 = 1 \implies \tfrac54 s^2 - 3s + 1 = 0 \implies 5s^2 - 12s + 4 = 0.$$

So $s = \frac{12 \pm 8}{10}$, i.e. $s = 2$ (a square whose top corners are the highest points of the circles — not the small square in the picture) or $s = \frac25$.

**Answer: (A)**

solutions.title: Right triangle at the centre
solutions.body:
Join the centre $M = (1, 1)$ of the right circle to the corner $V = (\frac s2, s)$. The horizontal distance is $1 - \frac s2$ and the vertical distance $1 - s$, and $MV = 1$. Test the options: for $s = \frac25$: $0.8^2 + 0.6^2 = 0.64 + 0.36 = 1$ ✓ — a 3-4-5 triangle.

**Answer: (A)**

prompt: Thomas wants to write down pairwise different positive whole numbers, none of which should be bigger than 100. Their product should not be divisible by 54. How many numbers can he write down at most?

solutions.title: Control the factor 3
solutions.body:
$54 = 2\cdot 3^3$. Two strategies:

- Avoid the factor 2: only odd numbers, at most 50.
- Allow even numbers but keep the total exponent of 3 at most 2. There are $100 - 33 = 67$ numbers up to 100 not divisible by 3. We can add numbers with total 3-exponent $\le 2$: two multiples of 3 that are not multiples of 9 (e.g. 3 and 6), or one multiple of 9. The best is two more numbers: $67 + 2 = 69$.

Adding a third multiple of 3 would give $3^3$, and there are certainly even numbers present, so the product would be divisible by 54. Maximum: 69.

**Answer: (D) 69**

prompt: Two regular polygons with side length 1 lie on opposite sides of the common edge $AB$. One of them is the 15-sided polygon $ABC_1D_1E_1\dots$ and the other one is the $n$-sided polygon $ABC_2D_2E_2\dots$. For which value of $n$ is the distance between $C_1$ and $C_2$ exactly 1?

solutions.title: Angles at B
solutions.body:
$BC_1 = BC_2 = 1$, so if $C_1C_2 = 1$ then triangle $BC_1C_2$ is equilateral and $\angle C_1BC_2 = 60^\circ$.

Around $B$: the 15-gon's interior angle is $\frac{13\cdot 180^\circ}{15} = 156^\circ$ and the $n$-gon's is $180^\circ - \frac{360^\circ}{n}$. Hence

$$156^\circ + 180^\circ - \frac{360^\circ}{n} + 60^\circ = 360^\circ \implies \frac{360^\circ}{n} = 36^\circ \implies n = 10.$$

**Answer: (A) 10**

prompt: The chain of equations $k = (2014 + m)^{\frac1n} = 1024^{\frac1n} + 1$ should be valid for the positive whole numbers $k$, $m$, $n$. How many different values can $m$ assume?

In the diagram a closed polygon can be seen whose vertices are the midpoints of the edges of the die. The interior angles are, as usual, defined as the angle that two sides of the polygon describe in a common vertex. What is the sum of all interior angles of the polygon?

solutions.title: Angles at edge midpoints
solutions.body:
The polygon passes through all 12 edge midpoints; each side joins the midpoints of two edges meeting at a corner of the cube (length $\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$ for edge 1).

At a midpoint $M$ the two sides go to midpoints of neighbouring edges. Placing the cube as $[0,1]^3$ and $M = (\frac12, 0, 0)$, the possible neighbours are $(0,\frac12,0)$, $(0,0,\frac12)$, $(1,\frac12,0)$, $(1,0,\frac12)$. The angle between the two sides is

- $60^\circ$ if both neighbours are at the same end of the edge,
- $90^\circ$ if they are at different ends but on the same face,
- $120^\circ$ if they are at different ends and on different faces.

Following the polygon in the picture, the turns alternate: $60^\circ, 120^\circ, 60^\circ, 120^\circ, \dots$ (each time the path turns around a corner of the cube, then crosses to the next face). Six angles of each kind: $6\cdot 60^\circ + 6\cdot 120^\circ = 1080^\circ$.

**Answer: (B) 1080°**

prompt: The mapping $f:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z$ fulfils the conditions $f(4) = 6$ and $x f(x) = (x-3) f(x+1)$. What is the value of the expression $f(4)\times f(7)\times f(10)\times\dots\times f(2011)\times f(2014)$?

solutions.title: Find a formula
solutions.body:
From $f(x+1) = \frac{x}{x-3}f(x)$: $f(5) = 4\cdot 6 = 24$, $f(6) = \frac52\cdot 24 = 60$, $f(7) = \frac63\cdot 60 = 120$. These are $3\cdot2\cdot1$, $4\cdot3\cdot2$, $5\cdot4\cdot3$, $6\cdot5\cdot4$, suggesting $f(x) = (x-1)(x-2)(x-3)$ for $x \ge 4$. Indeed $\frac{f(x+1)}{f(x)} = \frac{x(x-1)(x-2)}{(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)} = \frac{x}{x-3}$, and $f(4) = 6$.

Then

$$f(4)f(7)\cdots f(2014) = (3\cdot2\cdot1)(6\cdot5\cdot4)\cdots(2013\cdot2012\cdot2011) = 2013!$$

**Answer: (D) 2013!**

prompt: In the forests of a magical island kingdom there are three kinds of animals: lions, wolves and goats. Wolves can eat goats, and lions can eat wolves as well as goats. Since it is a magical island kingdom, the wolf that eats a goat changes into a lion. A lion that eats a goat changes into a wolf, and a lion that eats a wolf changes into a goat. To begin with there were 17 goats, 55 wolves and 6 lions on the island. After some time no more eating is possible. What is the maximum number of animals that can still be on the island?

solutions.title: Count the meals
solutions.body:
Let $a$ = wolf eats goat ($G-1, W-1, L+1$), $b$ = lion eats goat ($G-1, W+1, L-1$), $c$ = lion eats wolf ($G+1, W-1, L-1$).

When no eating is possible, at most one kind of animal is left. Every meal changes all three counts by $\pm1$, so the parities of $G - W$ (even at the start: $17 - 55$) and $W - L$ (odd: $55 - 6$) never change. Only goats left: $W - L = 0$, even ✗. Only wolves: $G - W$ and $W - L$ would be $-x$ and $x$, same parity ✗. So only lions remain.

Then $17 - a - b + c = 0$ and $55 - a + b - c = 0$. Adding: $a = 36$, and $c = b + 19$. The number of lions is $6 + a - b - c = 23 - 2b$, at most $23$ (with $b = 0$).

This is achievable: let lions eat wolves to create goats and let wolves eat goats, e.g. first 17 times a wolf eats a goat (lions $6 \to 23$, wolves $55 \to 38$, goats 0), then 19 times: a lion eats a wolf (new goat), and a wolf eats that goat (new lion). Each pair removes 2 wolves; after 19 pairs: 0 goats, 0 wolves, 23 lions.

**Answer: (D) 23**
